verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents resource monitors that track credit usage and can auto-suspend a warehouse (or disable an Adaptive Warehouse) when it hits a credit limit, warehouses that auto-suspend/auto-resume and can be started/stopped anytime, per-user quotas (GA), and newer cost-anomaly detection with notification integrations (GA) plus anomaly monitors (preview) — directly matching the 'stop a runaway query or idle compute overnight' story. Community evidence corroborates real-world use of resource monitors as a recommended cost-control practice, though one commenter notes Snowflake lacks query-level cost attribution/recommendations, a real secondary gap. Missing for 10: independent hands-on validation that auto-suspend/resource-monitor limits reliably halt a genuinely runaway single query mid-execution (vs. just capping warehouse-level spend), and more detail on the maturity of the preview anomaly-monitor feature.
